name: Montenegro: Kotor and the Bay, Budva and the coast, Durmitor

destination.name: Montenegro: Kotor and the Bay, Budva and the coast, Durmitor
destination.pitch: A country the size of Connecticut that fits a fjord-shaped bay, a 2,500m karst massif, a canyon you raft and a lake full of carp inside eight days, provided you rent a car and come in June or September rather than August.

because.nature: The Bay of Kotor is a drowned river valley with 1,000m walls, Durmitor has 18 glacial lakes and a 1,300m deep canyon, and Skadar is the biggest lake in the Balkans with pelicans in it.
because.exploration: Stone villages at 900m where the pršut is still smoked at home, an abandoned Ottoman town at Stari Bar, a river port at Rijeka Crnojevića that the railway killed, and a salt pan with flamingos that nobody visits.
because.food: Njeguški pršut and cheese from the smokehouses that make it, mussels and grilled fish in the bay konobas, lake carp and eel under a stone bridge, and kačamak with kajmak at 1,450m in Zabljak.
because.relaxation: The Dobrota quay at dusk, a pebble cove at Mogren before 09:00, a Pržno konoba table and Velika Plaža with a kilometre of shallow water; not in August and not in Budva after dark.
because.culture: A UNESCO walled town with a 1166 cathedral, a former royal capital of pastel embassies, Perast's baroque captains' houses and a mausoleum on a 1,657m summit.
because.adventure: Class III to IV rafting on the Tara, Bobotov Kuk at 2,523m with cables on the last scramble, 1,350 steps to the Kotor fortress and 25 hairpins up the serpentine.
because.city: Kotor and Budva are towns, not cities, and Podgorica is not worth a night; the urban part of this trip is two evenings inside old walls.

destination.caveat: The coast road is one lane each way and stops dead in August, Kotor to Zabljak is three and a half hours of hairpins each way, the Old Town in Kotor is a queue on a three-ship day, and the Durmitor ring road and the Tara rafting season only run from late May or June to October. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Kotor
cities.base: Dobrota, the 4km of waterfront north of the walls. You get a quay to walk and swim from, parking, and a 15 minute walk or a 3 euro taxi to the Sea Gate, and you are outside the Old Town when three cru

cities.name: Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks
cities.base: There are a dozen rooms in converted palaces but nobody needs a night here; it is 14km and 25 minutes from Kotor by the bay road, the Blue Line bus is 2 euros, and the whole village plus the islet is

cities.name: Lovćen National Park and Njeguši
cities.base: A mountain park with a mausoleum on top and a pršut village on the way up. There is nowhere to sleep at the summit and no reason to sleep in Njeguši. Do it as the day between Kotor and Cetinje: up the

cities.name: Cetinje
cities.base: Anywhere within 500m of Njegoševa ulica; the town is ten streets and every museum is a five minute walk. It is 670m up, so ten degrees cooler than the coast in summer, quiet by 22:00, and the right be

cities.name: Skadar Lake: Rijeka Crnojevića and Virpazar
cities.base: A national park lake with two villages on it, a river port at the north arm and a boat village at the south. Guesthouses exist in Virpazar but it is a lunch and a boat, not a night. From Cetinje it is

cities.name: Budva
cities.base: Inside the Old Town walls if you want the sea and the Mogren path at your door and can sleep through bass; the streets just west of the walls above the Mogren path if you cannot. Not Slovenska obala a

cities.name: Sveti Stefan and Pržno
cities.base: The island is a hotel, reopened by Aman in 2026 after five years shut, and the only beds on it start north of 1,000 euros. Everyone else sees it from the lay-by, swims on the public south beach and ea

cities.name: Ulcinj
cities.base: A guesthouse inside or just under the Old Town walls above Mala Plaža, where the evening is the cafes below the citadel and the sea is a five minute walk. The Velika Plaža strip is 5km out, a car ride

cities.name: Žabljak and Durmitor
cities.base: A pension or wooden cabin on the west side of town toward the Black Lake road, 1,450m up, with parking. Zabljak is a ski resort in a field, not pretty, and it does not need to be; the point is that Bl

cities.name: The Tara canyon and Šćepan Polje
cities.base: The deepest canyon in Europe at 1,300m and the rafting that runs its last 30km. The put-in and the camps sit at the Bosnian border, 70km and 75 minutes from Zabljak through the Piva canyon; the camps

outings.name: The Kotor ladder and the San Giovanni walls
outings.why: Up the old mule road behind the north gate, 70 switchbacks to the ruined hamlet of Špiljari, through the hole in the wall into the fortress at 280m, and down the 1,350 steps of the walls to the Old Town. Start at 07:00: by 10:00 on a cruise
outings.season: All year. July and August only before 09:00.
outings.fallback: The walls alone as far as the Church of Our Lady of Remedy at 650 steps, an hour, and the Maritime Museum after.

outings.name: Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks
outings.why: The bay road to Perast, the 5 euro boat to the islet and its 20 minute museum tour, the campanile, and grilled fish on the quay. It is a half day and the only difficulty is timing: the coaches from Kotor land at 10:30 and stay until 15:00.
outings.season: All year for the islet; the quay restaurants shut roughly No
outings.fallback: Konoba Ćatovića Mlini in Morinj, 10 minutes further, is a long lunch in a walled garden that does not care about rain.

outings.name: The serpentine, Njeguši lunch and the Lovćen mausoleum
outings.why: 25 hairpins out of Kotor to Krstac at 965m, pršut and cheese at Kod Pera in Njeguši, then 461 steps to the tomb on Jezerski vrh at 1,657m and the view over half the country. The road is paved and narrow and coaches use it after 09:30; the s
outings.season: April to November; the summit road can be snowed shut Decemb
outings.fallback: Njeguši and the Krstac viewpoint only, three hours, and the Cetinje museums in the afternoon.

outings.name: The Cetinje museums
outings.why: King Nikola's palace, Biljarda and the relief map, the History and Art Museum and the monastery, all within 400m and all on one 20 euro ticket. Flat, indoor, and the museums shut at 17:00, so this is a morning; the difficulty is that Cetinj
outings.season: All year. Winter hours end at 16:00.
outings.fallback: It is already the rain day.

outings.name: Skadar Lake: Pavlova Strana, Rijeka Crnojevića and the Virpazar boat
outings.why: Down the single track road from Cetinje to the river port, the horseshoe bend from the Pavlova Strana lay-by, then round to Virpazar for a 2.5 hour boat through the lilies and carp for lunch. May and June are the months, for the lilies and
outings.season: April to October for the boats; the restaurants run all year
outings.fallback: Lunch at Stari Most in Rijeka Crnojevića and the Besac fort above Virpazar, no boat, five hours.

outings.name: Budva Old Town and the Mogren coves
outings.why: The walled town in 40 minutes, the Citadela ramparts, then the cliff path to Mogren I and through the tunnel to Mogren II for the swim. Free pebbles are gone by 10:00 from July to early September and the path back in the afternoon is a proc
outings.season: Swimming June to early October; the Old Town all year.
outings.fallback: The Archaeological Museum and Konoba Stari Grad's terrace if the sea is up and the Mogren path is closed.

outings.name: Sveti Stefan and the Miločer walk to Pržno
outings.why: The photograph from the lay-by, a swim off the free south beach, the 25 minute pine walk through the old royal park to Pržno, and fish at Langust. You cannot walk onto the island unless you book one of the two daily Aman tours or a table at
outings.season: May to October; the island tours and the beach concessions s
outings.fallback: Pržno alone for lunch and the walk, two hours.

outings.name: Ulcinj: Velika Plaža, the Bojana and Ada
outings.why: The 12km beach by car, stopping wherever the sand is empty, fish soup at Miško on the river, the stilt huts and the Ada Bojana gate, and back up to the citadel for sunset. From Budva add 75 minutes each way and it becomes a nine hour day; t
outings.season: May to October. Ada and the beach clubs are shut from Novemb
outings.fallback: The Solana salt pans on foot in the morning and the Old Town museum, both fine in wind.

outings.name: Stari Bar and the old olive
outings.why: Two hours in an abandoned town of 250 ruins on a crag, 5 euros, then the 2,000 year old olive at Mirovica and ćevapi in the bazaar lane under the gate. It is on the road between Budva and Ulcinj, so it costs nothing extra; the crag is expos
outings.fallback: Konoba Kaldrma for lunch and the olive tree, an hour.

outings.name: Black Lake and Zminje jezero
outings.why: The 3.5km flat loop round the two Black Lakes under Međed, 3km from town, then 40 minutes on through pine forest to Snake Lake where nobody goes. One park ticket covers both. Before 09:00 or after 17:00 in August, or the first kilometre is
outings.season: May to October on foot; the lake freezes and the loop is sno
outings.fallback: It is the fallback. The lake loop alone is an hour in rain.

outings.name: The Durmitor ring
outings.why: The 76km one lane loop from Zabljak over Sedlo at 1,907m, down through Dobri Do and Trsa and back past Pišče, with the Prutaš and Sedlena Greda walls above you and no fuel anywhere on it. Counterclockwise, a full tank, and a stop at Sedlo f
outings.season: June to October. Closed by snow the rest of the year.
outings.fallback: The 20km to Sedlo pass and back the same way when the far side is fogged or the road is still shut.

outings.name: Bobotov Kuk from Sedlo
outings.why: The 2,523m summit by the short route from the pass: 616m of gain, 5 to 6 hours moving, scree, a cabled scramble at the top and no water on the way. Start from Sedlo by 08:00 because storms build after 14:00 from July and the descent on wet
outings.season: Mid June to early October. Snow in the gullies into June.
outings.fallback: Ćurevac over the Tara canyon, a 20 minute walk from the road end, and the Savin Kuk chairlift.

outings.name: Tara rafting from Šćepan Polje
outings.why: The van from Zabljak at 07:30 through the Piva canyon, then the full 30km from Splavište past Brstanovica to the Bosnian border, class III to IV, five to six hours in the boat with lamb from the sač at a camp after. 80 to 100 euros from Zab
outings.fallback: The half day from Splavište to Brstanovica, 12km of class II to III, about six hours door to door from Zabljak.

outings.name: Ćurevac and the Tara bridge
outings.why: The 20 minute walk from the Ćurevac road end to a balcony 1,000m over the canyon, then 22km to the Đurđevića Tara arch for the view and, if you want it, the zipline. The bridge is shut to all traffic for restoration from 10 August to 26 Oct
outings.season: May to October for the road to Ćurevac.
outings.fallback: The Bare Žugića stećci meadow, 10 minutes from town, and coffee at Or'O.

places.name: Old Town from the Sea Gate
places.note: Venetian walls, three squares and a street plan that loses everyone within five minutes; on a cruise day the Sea Gate is a queue by 09:00, so be inside before 08:30 or come back after 17:30 when the ships leave.

places.name: Cathedral of St Tryphon
places.note: Consecrated in 1166, with a reliquary chapel upstairs holding the saint's skull in a silver casket; the 4 euro ticket is fair, shoulders and knees must be covered, and the hours shorten in winter.

places.name: City walls to San Giovanni fortress
places.neighborhood: Stari Grad, above the north gate
places.note: 1,350 steps and 280m up for the view down the bay; 15 euros from a booth that is usually unmanned before 07:00, and by 10:00 on a ship day it is single file on hot stone with no shade.

places.name: The Ladder of Kotor to Špiljari
places.neighborhood: Trailhead behind the north gate on the Škurda
places.note: The old mule road to Cetinje, 70 switchbacks starting behind the river gate; a window in the fortress wall above the ruined hamlet of Špiljari lets you into the ramparts without a ticket, and nobody hurries you.

places.name: Maritime Museum of Montenegro
places.note: Three floors of the Grgurina palace on the Bokelj navy: ship models, weapons and portraits of captains; hours shrink to a morning on Sundays and out of season, so check the door before planning round it.

places.name: Kotor green market
places.neighborhood: Under the walls south of the Sea Gate
places.note: Njeguški cheese, pršut, figs and olives from stalls against the wall, best by 09:00; buy here rather than in the Old Town shops, which charge double for the same producers.

places.name: Konoba Scala Santa
places.note: Family run and the oldest konoba inside the walls, with pršut, black risotto and mussels buzara; no reservations, so eat before 19:00 or after 21:00 in summer.

places.name: Galion
places.neighborhood: The waterfront south of the walls, by the port
places.note: Kotor's dressed up fish dinner with the lit walls across the water; book for June to September and expect 35 to 60 euros a head before wine.

places.name: Konoba Ćatovića Mlini, Morinj
places.neighborhood: Morinj, 25 minutes west on the bay road
places.note: The bay's best known konoba, in a watermill garden with the mill stream through it: mussels, fish brodet, the pršut plate, and a July or August table only with a booking.

places.name: Bokun wine bar
places.note: Vranac and Krstač by the glass with a pršut board on a tiny square; the honest way to drink inside the walls without piazza prices.

places.name: Dobrota waterfront walk
places.note: Four kilometres of stone quay and captains' houses north of the walls, where Kotor people swim and walk at dusk; flat, free, and out of sight of the ships.

places.name: Blue Cave and Mamula speedboat
places.note: Three hours bouncing across the whole bay in a full RIB to a cave that is blue for ten minutes around midday; from Kotor it is the wrong end of the bay, and the Herceg Novi boats are shorter and cheaper.

places.name: Perast waterfront and the Bujović palaces
places.note: One street of baroque captains' houses facing the strait, no cars, and a stone quay you can swim off; arrive by 09:30, before the Kotor coaches stack up on the bypass.

places.name: Our Lady of the Rocks
places.note: A man-made islet with a 1630s church and a museum of 2,000 silver votive plaques; the 5 euro boat from the quay leaves when full and the 2 euro museum tour is 20 minutes, so the whole thing is an hour.

places.name: St Nicholas church tower
places.note: The 55m unfinished campanile from 1691, a couple of euros to climb, gives the view of both islets that the postcards use; the church treasury beside it is small.

places.name: Perast Museum in the Bujović palace
places.neighborhood: Perast, west end of the quay
places.note: A 1694 palace with portraits, ship models and the Venetian flags of a town that trained Peter the Great's naval cadets; closes at 14:00 or so in winter.

places.name: Konoba Školji
places.neighborhood: Perast, west end of the quay
places.note: Charcoal grilled fish on a terrace over the water with the islet in front of you; shut roughly November to March, like most of Perast.

places.name: Restaurant Conte
places.note: The fish is shown to you on a tray and priced by the kilo, so ask before you nod; the pontoon tables at sunset are the reason to pay it.

places.name: Fašinada, 22 July
places.note: Every 22 July at sunset the men of Perast row out in a chain of boats and throw stones onto the islet, as they have since 1452; one evening a year, so only relevant if the dates match.

places.name: The Kotor serpentine
places.neighborhood: The old Cetinje road from Škaljari to Krstac
places.note: 25 numbered hairpins climbing 900m out of Kotor with the whole bay below; paved, a lane and a half wide, and coaches use it after 09:30, so go up early and pull in only at the marked bends.

places.name: Krstac pass viewpoint
places.note: The top of the serpentine at 965m, a restaurant lay-by and the bay in one piece; the light is best before the haze comes up at midday.

places.name: Njeguši village
places.note: The Petrović dynasty's village at 900m where the stone smokehouses line the road and the same families have sold pršut out of the same houses for generations; cold, plain and honest.

places.name: Kafana Kod Pera na Bukovicu
places.note: The pršut, cheese and honey board people drive up for, 15 to 20 euros a head on a terrace over the karst, with the family smokehouse behind it; before 11:00 or after 14:30 in summer or you share it with a coach.

places.name: Njeguši smokehouse shop
places.note: A vacuum packed kilo of pršut for about 25 euros and a wheel of Njeguški cheese straight from a smokehouse door; it survives the flight and beats anything sold in Kotor.

places.name: Njegoš Mausoleum on Jezerski vrh
places.note: 461 steps through a tunnel to Meštrović's black granite tomb at 1,657m and a view of a third of the country; 8 euros plus the 3 euro park ticket, closes at 16:00 in winter, and cloud sits on it more afternoons than the brochures admit.

places.name: Ivanova Korita
places.note: The park's picnic meadow at 1,260m with beech shade, a spring and short marked loops; where Cetinje families go on a hot Sunday, and the one flat walk in the park.

places.name: Cetinje Monastery
places.note: The 1701 seat of the prince bishops, with relics that draw Orthodox pilgrims all year; free, modest dress, no photographs inside, and the monks move you along.

places.name: King Nikola's Museum
places.note: The last king's palace kept as he left it in 1916, with the guided room by room visit included in the 8 euros; the best of the Cetinje museums and the one to do if you do only one.

places.name: Biljarda and the relief map
places.note: Njegoš's 1838 residence, named for the billiard table carried up from Kotor on men's backs, and beside it a 1917 Austrian relief map of the whole country under glass; 5 euros for both.

places.name: History and Art Museum in Vladin dom
places.note: The old government building, with the icon of Our Lady of Philermos in a dark room upstairs and a floor on a state that fought everyone; the 20 euro all museums ticket pays if you do three.

places.name: Njegoševa ulica and the old embassies
places.note: The pedestrian main street of a capital that was a village, lined with the pastel embassies of powers that took Montenegro seriously for 40 years, and the town's cafes.

places.name: Ćipur court church
places.note: The 1890 court chapel where King Nikola and Queen Milena were reburied in 1989 after 68 years in Italy; five minutes, on the way between the palace and the monastery.

places.name: Orlov krš
places.note: Eagle's Crag, a 15 minute path up behind the monastery to the tomb of Danilo I with the whole town laid out below; free, and empty at dusk.

places.name: Lipa Cave
places.note: A 2.5km show cave with a road train to the mouth and a guided hour underground at 10 degrees; April to October, tours on the hour, and the wet cold is real.

places.name: Gradska kafana
places.note: The town cafe in a former embassy, breakfast for a few euros, Njeguški steak at lunch, and the whole of Cetinje passing the terrace.

places.name: Restoran Kole
places.note: Where locals take visitors: Njeguški steak stuffed with pršut and cheese, kačamak, plates big enough to share and no tourist pricing.

places.name: Belveder viewpoint
places.note: A roadside balcony where Skadar Lake and the whole delta open up 400m below; a stop on the way to Rijeka Crnojevića, not a trip.

places.name: Pavlova Strana viewpoint
places.neighborhood: On the Rijeka Crnojevića to Virpazar road
places.note: The horseshoe bend of the Crnojević river from a bend in the road above it, 10 minutes from the village; morning light, and the road is single track with drops and no barrier.

places.name: Rijeka Crnojevića and Danilo's bridge
places.note: A stone bridge from 1853 and one street of a river port that has been dying gently since the railway came; ten minutes to see, an hour to sit by the water.

places.name: Stari Most, Rijeka Crnojevića
places.note: Carp, eel and smoked bleak by the bridge from a family that has cooked lake fish here for decades; slow service, and the eel is the thing to order.

places.name: Virpazar
places.note: A three street lake village with a bridge, a fort and a line of boatmen calling from the quay; the launch point, not the sight.

places.name: A Virpazar boat into the lily fields
places.note: Two to three hours in a small open boat through the reeds and lilies to open water, with pelicans if you are lucky, 20 to 30 euros a head shared; go by 09:00, the afternoon is a glare and the lilies are a May and June thing.

places.name: Konoba Badanj, Virpazar
places.note: Carp from the oven, bleak fried whole and Crmnica Vranac in a stone room by the bridge; the reliable lunch after the boat.

places.name: Besac fortress
places.note: A 1478 Ottoman fort restored in 2013 on the hill over Virpazar, ten minutes up, a couple of euros, and the best view of the lake edge that does not need a boat.

places.name: Godinje wine village
places.note: A 14th century village of stone houses joined by passages, above terraced vines; knock at a cellar and the families pour Vranac for a few euros, and there is no sign for any of it.

places.name: Murići beach
places.neighborhood: The south shore below the Krajina villages
places.note: The lake's one proper beach, 40 minutes of narrow road from Virpazar, warm shallow water and a monastery on the island opposite; there is a campsite bar and nothing else.

places.name: Budva Old Town
places.note: A Venetian walled town rebuilt stone by stone after the 1979 earthquake, small enough to cover in 40 minutes; in July and August the lanes are a shuffle by 11:00 and the bars run until 02:00.

places.name: Citadela
places.note: A 4 euro fortress with a library, a room of ship models and the best rampart view over the roofs to Sveti Nikola island; closes around 17:00 outside June to September.

places.name: Trg između crkava
places.note: Three churches on one square, Orthodox Holy Trinity, Catholic St John, and Santa Maria in Punta from 840; five minutes, free, and the point where Budva stops being only bars.

places.name: Budva Archaeological Museum
places.note: Greek and Roman gold and glass from the necropolis under the modern town, on four small floors; the best 45 minutes of rain cover in Budva, and the hours change with the season so check the door.

places.name: Mogren beaches
places.neighborhood: West of the walls, along the cliff path
places.note: Two pebble coves 10 minutes along a cliff path from the Old Town, joined by a tunnel, past the Ballerina statue and its photo queue; the free stretch fills by 10:00 in summer, sunbeds run 15 to 25 euros a pair, and the path shuts after storms.

places.name: Konoba Stari Grad
places.note: A terrace through the back wall straight onto the sea and a fish menu that is fair for the Old Town; book the terrace in summer or you eat inside.

places.name: Jadran kod Krsta
places.note: A big family restaurant on the harbour promenade that Budva people still use: grilled fish, ćevapi, riblja čorba, and no theatre.

places.name: Casper Bar
places.note: A courtyard under a fig tree with jazz and DJs some nights, the one place inside the walls to drink without a beach club soundtrack.

places.name: Top Hill
places.neighborhood: Topliški put, the hill above town
places.note: An open air club for 5,000 on the hill behind town with international DJs, July and August only from about 23:00; loud enough that half of Budva hears it from bed.

places.name: Slovenska plaža
places.note: 1.6km of town beach behind a wall of sunbeds and speakers; in August it is elbow to elbow and the water is the worst on this stretch of coast.

places.name: Jaz beach
places.note: A kilometre of pebble and sand in a bowl of hills with a quiet west end and a beach club east end; the Sea Dance festival takes it over for a weekend in late August.

places.name: Sveti Nikola island by water taxi
places.note: Water taxis from the harbour run 5 to 8 euros return to a rocky island a kilometre out; the coves are small and the bar charges island prices, so go for the swim, not the day.

places.name: Sveti Stefan viewpoint from the coast road
places.note: The photograph everyone takes, from a lay-by on the Adriatic highway; morning light, and a coach in the lay-by on any summer day.

places.name: Aman Sveti Stefan island tour
places.note: Since the 2026 reopening the island is open to non-guests only on two guided heritage tours a day, at 11:30 and 16:00, 25 euros and booked by email; otherwise you need a table at the hotel restaurant to cross the causeway.

places.name: Sveti Stefan public beach
places.note: Pink pebbles and clear water on the south side of the causeway, free on the towel section; the north side and Queen's Beach belong to the hotel, and a sunbed there costs more than lunch.

places.name: The Miločer park walk to Pržno
places.note: Twenty five minutes under old pines through the former royal park from the causeway to Pržno, with the only free views down onto King's and Queen's beaches.

places.name: Konoba Langust, Pržno
places.note: A fishing village konoba on the Pržno beach with grilled fish and black risotto, calmer than anything in Budva; open roughly April to October.

places.name: Ulcinj Old Town
places.note: An Illyrian, then pirate, then Ottoman citadel on a cliff over Mala Plaža, half ruin and half guesthouses; in the evening the Albanian speaking town below fills its cafes and the walls empty.

places.name: Ulcinj Museum on Slave Square
places.note: Archaeology and ethnography in the old church turned mosque on the square where captured slaves were once sold; small, cheap, and the hours slip, so knock.

places.name: Mala Plaža
places.note: The town's 350m sand cove under the citadel, warm, shallow and packed with families in August; swim early and leave it to them.

places.name: Velika Plaža
places.note: Twelve kilometres of grey sand shelving so gently you walk 100m to swim, beach clubs at the town end and kite schools at the far end; a car makes it, the bus does not, and the wind is up every afternoon.

places.name: A kitesurf lesson at the south end of Velika Plaža
places.note: The afternoon thermal from May to September is why the schools are here; a two to three hour beginner block runs 70 to 90 euros and the water stays waist deep for a kilometre out, which is the point.

places.name: Ada Bojana
places.neighborhood: The river island at the Albanian border
places.note: A triangular island of river sand at the Albanian border, a naturist resort since 1973 with a 2 to 3 euro gate; the interesting part is the stilt fishing huts on the river banks, not the beach, and it is shut November to April.

places.name: Restaurant Miško on the Bojana
places.neighborhood: The Bojana river bank, before the Ada bridge
places.note: Thirty years of fish soup in metal bowls and grilled river fish on a stilt terrace over the Bojana; open all year, and the reason to drive down here.

places.name: Antigona
places.neighborhood: Stari Grad, on the cliff edge
places.note: Two terraces on the citadel cliff with the sunset over Mala Plaža and a buzara that justifies the walk up; book a rail table.

places.name: Solana Ulcinj salt pans
places.neighborhood: East of town, gate at the old salt plant
places.note: Fifteen square kilometres of abandoned salt works, protected since 2019, that hold flamingos and 250 bird species; walk or cycle the dyke roads from the old plant gate, bring water, there is no shade at all.

places.name: Valdanos bay
places.note: A pebble cove in an olive grove said to be 1,000 years old, once a Yugoslav army resort and now half derelict; clear water, a rough track down and no sunbed rack.

places.name: Stari Bar
places.neighborhood: Stari Bar, 30 minutes north of Ulcinj
places.note: An abandoned Ottoman and Venetian town of 250 ruins on a crag, 5 euros, with an aqueduct, a clock tower and a hammam; no shade after 11:00, good ćevapi in the lane below the gate, and the 2,000 year old olive at Mirovica is a euro and ten minutes on the way past.

places.name: Konoba Kaldrma, Stari Bar
places.neighborhood: The bazaar lane under the Stari Bar gate
places.note: A lane konoba under the ruins with Albanian style japrak, lamb and čorba for under 20 euros; the quiet lunch between Budva and Ulcinj.

places.name: Black Lake (Crno jezero)
places.neighborhood: Durmitor National Park, 3km west of town
places.note: A 3.5km flat loop round two glacial lakes under Međed, 5 euro park ticket at the gate, rowboats 10 euros an hour; by 11:00 in August the first kilometre is a procession and the far lake is not.

places.name: Zminje jezero
places.neighborhood: Durmitor National Park, beyond Black Lake
places.note: Snake Lake, a 40 minute forest path on from Black Lake to a small dark tarn with nobody at it; covered by the same park ticket, and the best short walk in the park.

places.name: Sedlo pass
places.note: The 1,907m saddle on the ring road under Bobotov Kuk, the start of the summit path and the highest point you can drive to in the country; snow shuts the road from about November to late May.

places.name: Bobotov Kuk from Sedlo
places.note: 2,523m, 616m of gain and 5 to 6 hours from Sedlo, with cables on the last scramble and no water on the route; leave the pass by 08:00 because storms build after 14:00 from July.

places.name: Ćurevac viewpoint
places.neighborhood: North of town, above the Tara canyon
places.note: A 20 minute walk from the end of the road to a balcony 1,000m over the Tara canyon; late afternoon, when the sun is behind you and the coaches have gone.

places.name: Đurđevića Tara bridge
places.neighborhood: 22km east of town on the Pljevlja road
places.note: A 365m five arch bridge from 1940, 170m over the river, with cafes and free parking at the Zabljak end; closed to all traffic for restoration from 10 August to 26 October 2026, so it is a view rather than a crossing in that window.

places.name: Tara zipline at the bridge
places.note: Twenty seconds across the canyon on a cable beside the bridge, 20 euros standard or 45 for the long line; fun, brief, and it stops when the bridge works or the wind say so.

places.name: Savin Kuk chairlift
places.note: Two lifts to 2,313m for the plateau view without the climb, daily in July and August and weekends either side; the wind at the top is real and the lift shuts in it.

places.name: Bare Žugića stećci
places.neighborhood: On the Njegovuđa road, 10 minutes north
places.note: Three hundred medieval carved tombstones in a meadow, UNESCO listed in 2016, no gate and usually no one; the sort of thing you stop for on the way to Ćurevac.

places.name: Restoran Or'O
places.note: The dependable one in town, open seven days all year, with a Durmitor platter of cheese, pršut and kajmak and a real breakfast before an early start.

places.name: Dvorište
places.note: A courtyard place with kačamak, cicvara and lamb from the sač, cheaper than the hotel dining rooms; order the kačamak with kajmak before anything else, it is the point of Durmitor food.

places.name: Restoran Koliba, Savin Kuk
places.note: A log hut at the lift base with trout, lamb and priganice with honey; open June to September and December to March only, shut in between.

places.name: Full day Tara rafting to Šćepan Polje
places.note: The full 30km from Splavište to the Bosnian border, class III to IV, 5 to 6 hours on the water with lunch at Brstanovica, 80 to 100 euros from Zabljak including the van; late April to mid October, and May is wetsuit water.

places.name: Half day rafting from Splavište to Brstanovica
places.note: The 12km everyone does, class II to III, under two and a half hours in the raft with a swim stop, 50 to 70 euros from Zabljak; the same drive as the full day for half the river, so only choose it for children or a short day.

places.name: Camp Encijan lunch at Brstanovica
places.note: Every camp on the river serves the same thing after the rapids: lamb or veal from the sač, cabbage, bread and rakija, included in most full day prices; Encijan is the one at Brstanovica where the half day ends.

places.name: The Piva canyon road
places.note: The road from Zabljak drops through 56 tunnels cut into the cliff above the green Piva reservoir on the way to the rafting camps; it is the drive, not a stop, and the rafting vans take it anyway.

places.name: Piva Monastery
places.neighborhood: Above the Piva lake, near Plužine
places.note: A 1573 church with 1,260 square metres of frescoes, moved stone by stone up the hill between 1970 and 1982 when the dam flooded its valley; free, and 10 minutes off the road back from the rafting.
